# Step 1

```{r}

dim(`2002_Data`)
head(`2002_Data`)

```

```{r}
'2022_Data' <- read.csv("C:/Users/nweit/OneDrive/Desktop/PM566/Assignment 1 Data/2022 PM2.5 Data.csv")
dim(`2022_Data`)
head(`2022_Data`)
tail(`2022_Data`)
str(`2022_Data`)
summary(`2022_Data`)

'2022-DMPMC' <- `2022_Data`$Daily.Mean.PM2.5.Concentration
hist(`2022-DMPMC`,
     main = "Distribution of Daily Mean PM 2.5 Concentration (2022)",
     xlab = "Daily Mean PM 2.5 Concentration (micrograms per cubic meter)")
```

## Summary

While both datasets contain 22 variables, the 2002 dataset contains 15,976 observations and the 2022 dataset contains 59,918 observations. In 2002, the daily mean PM2.5 Concentration has a range of 0 to 104.3. In 2022, the daily mean PM2.5 Concentration has a range of -6.7 to 302.5, which may suggest an recording error, as PM2.5 Concentration values cannot be negative. The distributions of Daily Mean PM 2.5 Concentration between the two datasets are extremely different. According to the histograms and table views, in 2002, the majority of observations (4,101 or 25.7% of observations) lie within the 5-10 micrograms per cubic meter range, with a smooth drop off as concentration increases. In 2022, almost all observations (56,593 or 94.5% of observations) lie within the 0-20 micrograms per cubic meter range, with just a couple observations near 300 micrograms per cubic meter, and 343 observations lying in the -20 - 0 micrograms per cubic meter range. Both distributions are positively skewed, but it should be noted that the 2002 distribution ranges from 0 - 100 micrograms per cubic meter and the 2022 distribution ranges from -20 - 300 micrograms per cubic meter (before dataset cleaning).

# Step 2

```{r}
Combined_Data <- merge(`2002_Data`, `2022_Data`, all = TRUE)

Combined_Data$Date <- as.Date(Combined_Data$Date, format = "%m/%d/%Y")
Combined_Data$Year <- format(Combined_Data$Date, "%Y")

names(Combined_Data)[names(Combined_Data) == "Daily.Mean.PM2.5.Concentration"] <- "PM2.5"

head(Combined_Data)
tail(Combined_Data)
summary(Combined_Data)
```

# Step 3

```{r}
library(leaflet)

# sites: data.frame with lat, lng, year (hundreds of rows)

pal <- colorFactor(palette = c("#00FFFF", "#FF0000"), domain = Combined_Data$Year)

leaflet(Combined_Data) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addCircleMarkers(
    lng = Combined_Data$Site.Longitude, 
    lat = Combined_Data$Site.Latitude, 
    color = ~pal(Combined_Data$Year), 
    radius = 5,
    stroke = TRUE,
    weight = 0.5,
    fillOpacity = 0.5
  ) |>
  addLegend(
    position = "bottomleft",
    pal = pal,
    values = Combined_Data$Year,
    title = "Year",
    opacity = 1
  ) 
```

## Summary

Based on the map, it appears that the distribution has expanded from 2002 to 2022. Some sites overlap, meaning that they exist in both years, but there are considerably more 2022 sites(red) than 2002 sites (blue). The "hotspots" appear to be Southern California, the Bay Area, and the Sacramento Area, while Northern California and Mojave are sparsely populated with sites. This makes sense given that the former locations are densely populated and the latter are not.

# Step 4

```{r}
summary(Combined_Data)

colSums(is.na(Combined_Data))
colMeans(is.na(Combined_Data))

colSums(Combined_Data < 0)
sum(Combined_Data$PM2.5 < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
mean(Combined_Data$PM2.5 < 0, na.rm = TRUE)

flag_value <- is.na(Combined_Data$PM2.5) |
  Combined_Data$PM2.5 < 0

Proporption_2002 <- mean(flag_value[Combined_Data$Year == 2002])
Proporption_2022 <- mean(flag_value[Combined_Data$Year == 2022])

data.frame(Year = c(2002, 2022), Proportion_MI = 100 * c(Proporption_2002, Proporption_2022))
```

## Summary

When looking for missing values (N/A values), I found that the CBSA.Code column had 5,498 instances and all other variables had 0 instances. When looking at implausible values for the main variable, PM2.5, I found that 215 observations were below 0. I determined that any values below 0 were implausible because PM2.5 is measured in micrograms per cubic meter, meaning that the lowest possible value it could be is 0, as there cannot be negative micrograms per cubic meter of something. I did not classify those extremely high PM2.5 as implausible, as the concentration may rise to such levels in wildfires. The proportion of these implausible values differs between 2002 and 2022, with the former having 0 implausible values and the latter having \~0.36% of observations being implausible.

# Step 5

Main Question: Did daily concentrations of PM2.5 decreased in California over the 20 years spanning from 2002 to 2022?

## Level 1: State

```{r}
Summary_Data <- data.frame( 
  Year = as.numeric(as.character(Combined_Data$Year)),
  County = Combined_Data$County,
  Site = Combined_Data$Local.Site.Name,
  PM2.5 = as.numeric(as.character(Combined_Data$PM2.5))
  )

Summary_Data <- Summary_Data[
  !is.na(Summary_Data$PM2.5) &
  !is.na(Summary_Data$County) &
  !is.na(Summary_Data$Site) &
  !is.na(Summary_Data$Year) &
    Summary_Data$PM2.5 >= 0,
    ] 

State_Data <- Summary_Data[
  !is.na(Summary_Data$PM2.5) &
  !is.na(Summary_Data$County) &
  !is.na(Summary_Data$Site) &
    Summary_Data$PM2.5 >= 0,
    ]

by(State_Data$PM2.5, State_Data$Year, summary)

boxplot(PM2.5 ~ Year, data = State_Data)

PM2.5_2002 <- State_Data$PM2.5[State_Data$Year == 2002]
PM2.5_2022 <- State_Data$PM2.5[State_Data$Year == 2022]
hist(PM2.5_2002)
hist(PM2.5_2022)
```

### Summary

At the state level, the median and mean PM2.5 concentrations have decreased to about half that of the median and mean of PM2.5 concentrations in 2002. Along with that, most PM2.5 concentrations are more frequently in the 0-25 micrograms per cubic meter in 2022, which shows improvement from 2002, where concentrations ranged from 0 to 100.

## Level 2: County

```{r}
County_Data <- Summary_Data[
  !is.na(Summary_Data$PM2.5) &
  !is.na(Summary_Data$County) &
  Summary_Data$PM2.5 >= 0,
]

County_Means <- aggregate(
  PM2.5 ~ County + Year,
  data = County_Data,
  FUN = mean
)

County_Means

by(Summary_Data$PM2.5, list(County = Summary_Data$County,Year = Summary_Data$Year), summary)

plot(
  NA,
  xlim = c(2000, 2025),
  ylim = range(County_Means$PM2.5, na.rm = TRUE),
  xaxt = "n",
  xlab = "Year",
  ylab = "Mean PM2.5 Concentration",
  main = "Change in Mean PM2.5 by County from 2002 to 2022"
)

axis(
  side = 1,
  at = c(2002, 2022),
  labels = c("2002", "2022")
)

County_List <- unique(County_Means$County)

for (County_Name in County_List) {
County_Values <- County_Means[County_Means$County == County_Name,]
if (
    2002 %in% County_Values$Year &&
    2022 %in% County_Values$Year
  ) {

    County_Values <- County_Values[
      order(County_Values$Year),
    ]

    lines(
      County_Values$Year,
      County_Values$PM2.5,
      type = "o",
      pch = 19,
      col = rgb(0.2, 0.4, 0.8, 0.5)
    )

    text(
      x = 2022.5,
      y = County_Values$PM2.5[
        County_Values$Year == 2022
      ],
      labels = County_Name,
      pos = 4,
      cex = 0.4
    )
  }
}

Means_2002 <- County_Means[
  County_Means$Year == 2002,
  c("County", "PM2.5")
]

Means_2022 <- County_Means[
  County_Means$Year == 2022,
  c("County", "PM2.5")
]

names(Means_2002)[2] <- "Mean_2002"
names(Means_2022)[2] <- "Mean_2022"

County_Comparison <- merge(
  Means_2002,
  Means_2022,
  by = "County"
)

County_Comparison$Change <-
  County_Comparison$Mean_2022 -
  County_Comparison$Mean_2002

County_Comparison <- County_Comparison[
  order(County_Comparison$Change),
]

plot_positions <- seq_len(nrow(County_Comparison))

par(mar = c(5, 10, 4, 2))

plot(
  NA,
  xlim = range(
    County_Comparison$Mean_2002,
    County_Comparison$Mean_2022
  ),
  ylim = c(0.5, nrow(County_Comparison) + 0.5),
  yaxt = "n",
  xlab = "Mean PM2.5 Concentration",
  ylab = "",
  main = "Change in County Mean PM2.5 Concentrations from 2002 to 2022"
)

axis(
  side = 2,
  at = plot_positions,
  labels = County_Comparison$County,
  las = 1,
  cex.axis = 0.65
)

segments(
  x0 = County_Comparison$Mean_2002,
  y0 = plot_positions,
  x1 = County_Comparison$Mean_2022,
  y1 = plot_positions,
  col = "gray",
  lwd = 2
)

points(
  County_Comparison$Mean_2002,
  plot_positions,
  pch = 19,
  col = "blue"
)

points(
  County_Comparison$Mean_2022,
  plot_positions,
  pch = 19,
  col = "red"
)

legend(
  "topright",
  legend = c("2002", "2022"),
  col = c("blue", "red"),
  pch = 19,
  bty = "n"
)

par(mar = c(5, 4, 4, 2) + 0.1)
```

## Summary

Based on the graph, it appears that the mean PM2.5 concentrations have decreased from 2002 to 2022 in most counties. There are a total of six counties that had an increase in mean PM2.5 concentrations since 2002.

## Level 3: City

```{r}
unique(
  Summary_Data$County[
    grepl(
      "Los Angeles",
      Summary_Data$County,
      ignore.case = TRUE
    )
  ]
)

LA_Data <- Summary_Data[
  Summary_Data$County == "Los Angeles" &
  Summary_Data$Year %in% c(2002, 2022) &
  !is.na(Summary_Data$Site) &
  !is.na(Summary_Data$PM2.5) &
    trimws(as.character(Summary_Data$Site)) != "" &
  Summary_Data$PM2.5 >= 0,
]

LA_Data <- droplevels(LA_Data)

unique(LA_Data$Site)
table(LA_Data$Site, LA_Data$Year)
Site_Means <- aggregate(
  PM2.5 ~ Site + Year,
  data = LA_Data,
  FUN = mean
)

Site_Means

by(LA_Data$PM2.5,list(Site = LA_Data$Site,Year = LA_Data$Year),
  summary
)

Site_Means <- aggregate(
  PM2.5 ~ Site + Year,
  data = LA_Data,
  FUN = mean
)

Sites_2002 <- Site_Means[
  Site_Means$Year == 2002,
  c("Site", "PM2.5")
]

Sites_2022 <- Site_Means[
  Site_Means$Year == 2022,
  c("Site", "PM2.5")
]

names(Sites_2002)[2] <- "Mean_2002"
names(Sites_2022)[2] <- "Mean_2022"

Site_Comparison <- merge(
  Sites_2002,
  Sites_2022,
  by = "Site"
)

Site_Comparison$Change <-
  Site_Comparison$Mean_2022 -
  Site_Comparison$Mean_2002

Site_Comparison <- Site_Comparison[
  order(Site_Comparison$Change),
]

positions <- seq_len(nrow(Site_Comparison))

par(mar = c(5, 10, 4, 2))

plot(
  NA,
  xlim = range(
    Site_Comparison$Mean_2002,
    Site_Comparison$Mean_2022
  ),
  ylim = c(0.5, nrow(Site_Comparison) + 0.5),
  yaxt = "n",
  xlab = "Mean PM2.5 Concentration",
  ylab = "",
  main = "Comparison of Mean PM2.5 Concentration in Los Angeles County Sites from 2002 and 2022"
)

axis(
  side = 2,
  at = positions,
  labels = Site_Comparison$Site,
  las = 1,
  cex.axis = 0.7
)

segments(
  x0 = Site_Comparison$Mean_2002,
  y0 = positions,
  x1 = Site_Comparison$Mean_2022,
  y1 = positions,
  col = "gray",
  lwd = 2
)

points(
  Site_Comparison$Mean_2002,
  positions,
  pch = 19,
  col = "blue",
  cex = 1.2
)

points(
  Site_Comparison$Mean_2022,
  positions,
  pch = 19,
  col = "red",
  cex = 1.2
)

legend(
  "topright",
  legend = c("2002", "2022"),
  col = c("blue", "red"),
  pch = 19,
  bty = "n"
)

par(mar = c(5, 4, 4, 2) + 0.1)
```

## Summary

Based on the graph, it appears that all the sites in Los Angeles county have shown decreases in mean PM2.5 concentrations since 2002.
